novelty.justification: The claim predicts that models "allocate more thinking tokens ... on the exact same problem when the questioner is framed as high social status" and posits a "status-sensitive effort-budget representation read at the prompt boundary," making its novelty route a new social-conditioning relationship and mechanistic interpretation of adaptive reasoning effort. Searches using "LLM user status reasoning tokens compute allocation," "authority bias chain of thought length," "persona social status test-time compute," and "LLM effort budget representation activation patching" found adjacent work on authority/sycophancy effects and adaptive test-time compute—especially Sharma et al.'s 2023 sycophancy research and Snell et al.'s 2024 work on scaling test-time compute—but no verified work connecting questioner status to reasoning-token allocation or a causal internal budget signal; the submission's recent "Trust Me, I'm an Expert" citation could not be independently verified as of 2026-08-26. The step is therefore a non-trivial combination and operationalization rather than merely renaming a method, but it remains a natural extension of social-framing bias studies plus standard probing, activation patching, and steering, rather than a wholly new interpretability paradigm.
